tools.name: read_model
tools.description: Outlines the model: its sim specs; each stock with its initial value, inflows and outflows; the flows, computed variables, constants, lookup tables and modules, each with its equation and units; and the engine's diagnostics, each with an id (D1, D2, ...) that later calls and claims can cite. Also says what changed since you last read it. Read the model before saying anything about it.

inputSchema.title: ReadModelInput
inputSchema.description: `read_model` takes nothing: a session is bound to its model.

saveStep.description: How often results are saved, when it differs from DT.

Counts.description:
How many of each kind of variable the model has, and of each severity of
diagnostic: always whole, whatever the outline lists.

initial.description: The initial value's equation; absent in a sector outline.

VariableOutline.description: A flow or a computed auxiliary.

equation.description: The equation, cut at 240 characters (`truncated` says so).

lookup.description: The graphical function the equation's value is looked up in, if any.

LookupSummary.description: A graphical function's extent; `read_variables` has its points.

value.description: The value as written; for an arrayed constant, each element's.

ModuleInputOutline.description:
One wire into a module: the variable it reads, and the module's input it
feeds.

DiagnosticReport.description: A diagnostic as a tool reports it.

id.description: The session's id for this diagnostic (`D1`, ...), stable while it exists.

code.description: The engine's code for the class of failure, in snake_case.

variable.description:
The variable to fix, as the model names it; absent for a problem with
the model or the project as a whole.

reason.description:
Why, in words: the raising site's reason, and the text it points at
whenever it has a span; what its code means only when neither.

Severity.description: Whether a diagnostic stops the model from simulating or only warns.

DiagnosticCategoryName.description:
Where a diagnostic was raised, named for a reader: one per category of
the engine's (`DiagnosticCategory`).

oneOf.description:
An equation that does not parse, names something that does not
exist, or cannot be compiled.

A problem with the model as a whole: a cycle, a duplicate name, a bad
table.
A units string that does not parse.
An equation whose computed units disagree with its declared units.
A contradiction among the units the model's equations imply.
A construct the compiler refuses.

A value a run produces that is not a number: what an edit's gate
finds in the run, where the engine's diagnostics are silent.

Changes.description:
What changed since a read. Each list of variables is capped at 30 names,
and an outline cuts the lists further to fit its budget
([`Changes::fitted`]), with the total counted beside a list when either
binds.

sinceRevision.description: The revision the agent last read at.

specsChanged.description:
Whether the start, stop, DT, save step, integration method or time
units changed.

dimensionsChanged.description:
Whether the project's dimensions changed: an element added, removed
or renamed, or a dimension added or removed.

unitDefinitionsChanged.description: Whether the project's unit definitions changed.

modelsChanged.description:
The project's other models whose variables or sim specs changed (the
models a module instantiates among them), and those added or removed.

ChangedVariable.description: One variable whose record changed, and which of its fields did.

ChangedField.description: A variable's fields, as a change report names them.

oneOf.description: It became a different kind of variable (an auxiliary became a stock).
Its equation, or for a stock its initial value.
A module's model or its input wiring.

How its name is written, when only case or spacing changed; a rename
is a removal and an addition.

Anything else an import carries (an active initial value, a data
source, a conveyor or queue marker, visibility).

sectors.description:
The sectors left out; a sector with no variable is never listed and
is not counted.

revision.description: The project revision this outline read.

lookups.description: Standalone lookup tables, which other equations call.

changes.description: What changed since this session last read the model, when anything did.

sectors.description:
Present when the model is outlined by sector: its sectors that hold a
variable, each with how many it holds and which stocks.

otherNames.description:
In a sector outline, the names of the variables that are not stocks,
in model order, as many as fit beside the stocks.

omitted.description:
How many stocks, diagnostics, sectors and other names an outline left
out to keep to its budget.

note.description: What an outline by sector leaves to `read_variables`.

tools.name: read_variables
tools.description: Reads up to 12 variables whole: kind, units, documentation, equation or initial value, per-element equations, lookup points, a stock's flows or the stocks a flow fills and drains, the variables each reads and is read by with every link's polarity, and its diagnostic ids. A name that matches nothing comes back with the closest names.

VariableRecord.description: Everything a variable's definition holds, and its causal neighbors.

element.description:
The element read, when one was named (`population[north]`): the
record's equation or initial value is that element's.

equation.description:
A flow's or auxiliary's equation; absent for per-element equations,
which `elements` lists.

truncated.description:
Set when the equation, the initial value or `otherElements` was cut
(it then ends in an ellipsis) because the record did not fit one
answer whole.

initial.description: A stock's initial value; absent for per-element initial values.

elements.description:
Per-element equations (or a stock's per-element initial values): at
most 24, each cut at 240 characters and 2,400 in all; name an element
to read its equation whole.

moreElements.description: How many more per-element equations there are than `elements` lists.

otherElements.description: The equation of every element `elements` does not list.

inputs.description: The variables this one reads, each with its link's polarity, at most 24.

readers.description:
The variables that read this one, each with its link's polarity, at
most 24.

diagnostics.description: This variable's diagnostics, each under the id `read_model` gives it.

moreDiagnostics.description: How many more diagnostics it has than `diagnostics` lists.

behavior.description:
What it did in the current run: a scalar variable's start and end,
extremes and behavior mode (`read_behavior` has an arrayed one's, and
more).

VariableKind.description: What a variable is, as a modeler would say it.

oneOf.description: A computed auxiliary.
An auxiliary whose equation is a number.
A standalone table other equations call.
An instance of another model.

morePoints.description: How many more points the table has than are listed (at most 64).

oneOf.description: Interpolates between points and holds the end values beyond them.
Interpolates between points and extends the end segments beyond them.
Steps from point to point.

ModuleRecord.description: The wiring of a module instance.

ModuleInputOutline.description:
One wire into a module: the variable it reads, and the module's input it
feeds.

LinkRef.description: One end of a read, from the variable a record describes.

polarity.description:
The sign of the causal link; `?` for a read that is no causal link (a
table looked up, a read made only at the start).

startOnly.description:
Set when the read is made only as the model starts (a stock's initial
value, an `INIT` argument): it sets where the reader starts and does
not move it afterwards, so it is on no feedback loop.

option.description:
The stock's or flow's option the read is made in, when it is one: the
engine reads it there, outside the reader's equation.

unchecked.description:
Set when the read is written in an equation the engine cannot compile
(an unknown function, a wrong argument count): the reader reads it
once that equation compiles.

LinkPolarityName.description:
A link's sign as system dynamics writes it: `+` when the target moves with
the source, `-` when against it, `?` when the engine cannot tell from the
equation.

StockOptionName.description: A stock's or a flow's option, as a read record names it.

oneOf.description: A conveyor's transit time.
A conveyor's capacity.
A conveyor's inflow limit.
A conveyor's sample condition.
A conveyor's arrest condition.
A leak flow's fraction.
Where a leak's zone starts.
Where a leak's zone ends.

DiagnosticReport.description: A diagnostic as a tool reports it.

id.description: The session's id for this diagnostic (`D1`, ...), stable while it exists.

code.description: The engine's code for the class of failure, in snake_case.

variable.description:
The variable to fix, as the model names it; absent for a problem with
the model or the project as a whole.

reason.description:
Why, in words: the raising site's reason, and the text it points at
whenever it has a span; what its code means only when neither.

Severity.description: Whether a diagnostic stops the model from simulating or only warns.

DiagnosticCategoryName.description:
Where a diagnostic was raised, named for a reader: one per category of
the engine's (`DiagnosticCategory`).

oneOf.description:
An equation that does not parse, names something that does not
exist, or cannot be compiled.

A problem with the model as a whole: a cycle, a duplicate name, a bad
table.
A units string that does not parse.
An equation whose computed units disagree with its declared units.
A contradiction among the units the model's equations imply.
A construct the compiler refuses.

A value a run produces that is not a number: what an edit's gate

SeriesCore.description:
What a series did, in brief. A value that is not a number (a division by
zero, an overflow) is left out, as are a start, an end, a sample or a
turning point that is not one; the mode says when the series went
undefined.

Every number it reports is the series' own, rounded to five significant
digits, so every tool that reports a number of a series reports the same
one. Its parts agree with each other: a series that is not at rest
reports a least and a greatest value that read differently, and it went
negative exactly when a number reported of it is negative. A series that
is the residue of quantities that cancel (`behavior::classify_at`) is at
rest, and reports the residue it holds.

min.description: Its least and greatest values that are numbers, with their times.

negativeFrom.description: When it first went below zero, if it ever did.

direction.description:
Which way it moves: for an overshoot or a single turn, the way it
first went; absent at rest and for an oscillation.

startsAt.description: When a series that sat still at first began to move.

settlesAt.description: When a series stopped moving, if that was before the run ended.

oneOf.description: Does not move: an equilibrium.
Moves at a steady speed.
Moves ever faster: exponential growth, or an accelerating decline.
Moves ever slower toward a level: approach to a goal, or decay.
Speeds up, then slows toward a level.

Passes the level it ends at, and comes back less than half the way it
went.

Rises, peaks, and falls back more than half the way it rose: overshoot
and collapse.
Falls, bottoms, and rises back more than half the way it fell.
Swings back and forth.
Takes a non-finite value.
None of these.
Each swing smaller than the last.
Swings of about the same size.
Each swing larger than the last.
Too few swings in the run to tell.

suggestions.description: The closest names of variables, when no variable has the name.

reason.description:
Why not, when the variable exists and what was asked of it does not:
an element it does not have, or a subscript on a variable with none.

notFound.description: Names that matched no variable, each with the closest names.

omitted.description:
Variables left out to keep the answer within its budget, to read in
another call.

behaviorUnavailable.description: Why the records carry no behavior, when the model does not simulate.

tools.name: find_variables
tools.description: Finds variables by a name, part of a name, a misspelling, or a few words of description, closest first. Use it when a name the person said or wrote does not match the model's.

phrase.description:
A name, part of one (the starts of its words: "pop gr" finds
"population growth"), a misspelling, or a few words of description;
at most 256 characters. The name itself ranks first, then names whose
words the phrase starts, then names and descriptions like it; a
phrase under four characters finds only the first two.

score.description: How closely the phrase matches, from 0 to 1.

VariableKind.description: What a variable is, as a modeler would say it.

oneOf.description: A computed auxiliary.
An auxiliary whose equation is a number.
A standalone table other equations call.
An instance of another model.

omitted.description:
Matches left out, the least close, to keep the answer within its
budget: names too long to list them all.

tools.name: run_experiment
tools.description: Runs a what-if experiment on a copy of the model and keeps it under a name for later calls and claims to cite: set constants to values or multiply them, replace equations (which cuts the links from what they read: how to test an explanation), from a time on or from the start, and change DT, the integration method or the stop time. Returns each change as applied and each recorded variable's behavior beside the run it started from. The model itself is not changed.

ChangeInput.description: One change to one variable: its new value, a multiplier for its value, or a replacement equation.

value.description: A constant's new value (for an arrayed constant, every element's).

multiply.description: A factor for a constant's value in the run the experiment starts from.

equation.description: A replacement equation, in this run only; for a stock, its initial value. It replaces the variable's value, a table it fed included. Replacing a computed variable's equation cuts the links from what it read: that is how a link is taken out to test an explanation.

name.description:
A short name the run is kept and cited under; a name already used
replaces that run. "current" is the model as it is, and is not a name
an experiment can take.

from.description:
The run to start from and compare with: "current" (the default) or a
run an experiment made. Its changes are kept unless this experiment
changes the same variables.

set.description: The changes, each to one variable.

fromTime.description:
When the value and multiplier changes take effect: from the first step
at or after this time; from the start (initial values included) when
absent. Equation changes always hold from the start.

record.description:
The variables to summarize, by name; the model's stocks when absent.
At most 12.

value.description:
The value it took, and what it was in the starting run (a scalar
constant).

elements.description: Each element's value and what it was (an arrayed constant).

equation.description: The replacement equation, and the equation it replaced.

tableDropped.description:
That the variable's table no longer applies: its value was the table
at its equation's value, and is now the replacement itself.

saveStep.description: How often results are saved, when it differs from DT.

Comparison.description: A variable's behavior in the new run and in the run it started from.

base.description:
Absent when there is no run to compare with: the model as it is does
not simulate.

from.description: The run it started from and is compared with.

specs.description: The specs the run ran under.

behavior.description:
Each recorded variable (or element) in this run and in the one it

omitted.description:
Recorded variables and elements left out, when there were more than a

replaced.description: Whether the run replaced an earlier run of the same name.

forgotten.description: A run forgotten to keep the session within its runs.

tools.name: read_behavior
tools.description: Summarizes what variables did in runs: start and end, minimum and maximum with their times, turning points, when it first went negative, its behavior mode (at rest, linear, exponential, goal seeking, S-shaped, overshoot, rise and fall, fall and rise, oscillation, undefined for a non-finite value, or other), and a dozen samples. Name an element to read one (population[north]). "current" is the model as it is; other runs are experiments'.

variables.description:
The variables to summarize, by name, or one element of an arrayed
variable (`population[north]`); at most 12.

runs.description:
The runs to summarize them in, by name: "current" for the model as it
is, or runs an experiment made. "current" alone when absent; at most 4.

SeriesSummary.description: A variable's (or one element's) behavior in a run.

variable.description: The variable, with its element for an arrayed one (`population[north]`).

min.description: Its least and greatest values that are numbers, with their times.

negativeFrom.description: When it first went below zero, if it ever did.

turns.description:
Its turning points, the peaks and troughs it reversed from, in order;
at most six.

samples.description:
About a dozen evenly spaced values, first and last included; left out
when the answer is over its budget.

Which way it moves: for an overshoot or a single turn, the way it
first went; absent at rest and for an oscillation.

reason.description:
Why not, when the variable exists and what was asked of it does not:
an element it does not have, or a subscript on a variable with none.

LeftOut.description:
What a `read_behavior` answer left out to fit its budget, in the order it
leaves things out.

variables.description: Variables left out whole, to read in another call.

series.description: One summary per variable (or element) and run, variable by variable.

omittedElements.description:
Arrayed variables with more elements than a summary lists, and how
many were left out.

staleRuns.description:
Runs made before the model last changed (its diagrams aside): what
they show is what the model did then.

leftOut.description: What was left out to keep the answer within its budget.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: Lists the runs experiments made, oldest first, and says for each whether the model has changed since it was made and what it changed from the model: each constant's value (from a time on, or from the start), each replacement equation, the run specs, and the run it started from. Use it to learn what a run the person made, or one of yours from earlier, tried.

RunListing.description: What a session tells a host, or an agent, of one of its runs.

revision.description: The revision the run was made at.

stale.description: Whether the model has changed, beyond its diagrams, since.

gone.description: Whether the run is gone: stale, with its results no longer kept.

from.description:
The run it started from, as it was named then: "current", the model
as it was, or a run an experiment made.

changes.description:
Everything the run changed from the model, with the changes it kept
from the run it started from: values first, then equations.

specs.description: The run specs it changed; a spec left out is the model's.

ListedChange.description:
One change a run makes to one variable, as it was made: exactly the value
the run set, where the experiment's answer rounds it.

variable.description:
The variable as the model spells it, or its canonical name when the
model no longer has it.

elements.description:
An arrayed constant's value element by element, or an equation for
each element.

equation.description: A replacement equation, which holds from the start.

tableDropped.description:
That the replacement is the variable's value, where the model's
variable is a table read at its equation's value.

fromTime.description:
When a value takes effect: from the first step at or after this
time, or from the start (initial values included) when absent.

ListedElement.description: One element's value, or its replacement equation, in a listed change.

element.description: The element's subscript, as a results key spells it (`north`, `a,b`).

SpecsChange.description:
The specs a run ran under where they are not the model's; one left out
is the model's.

saveStep.description:
How often the run saves. An experiment keeps the model's; a battery
check that refines DT saves at the model's own times, so its rows
compare with the model's one for one and it holds no more than the
model's run does.

runs.description:
The session's named runs, oldest first. "current", the model as it
is, is always there and is not listed.

omitted.description: Runs left out to keep the answer within its budget, oldest first.

tools.name: analyze_loops
tools.description: Finds the feedback loops that drove a run, and when: for each group of stocks feedback connects, which loops led over the run and with what share, and the loops themselves, each with an id (L1, L2, ...) that later calls and claims can cite, its polarity (reinforcing or balancing) and its chain of links with their signs. Loops, their polarity and their dominance come from here. A run that holds still, as a model at equilibrium does, has no active loop: its loops come from structure, and an experiment that disturbs it shows which dominates. For an experiment that replaced equations, names the loops it cut.

run.description:
The run to analyze: "current" for the model as it is (when absent), or
a run an experiment made.

through.description:
Only the loops through this variable (any of its elements, or the one
named, as in `population[north]`), and the partitions they are in.

loops.description:
Loops to report whole, by the ids earlier answers gave them: each with
its full chain, in its partition, and no dominance timeline. At most
4, and not with `through`.

LoopBasis.description: Where an answer's loops come from.

oneOf.description:
The run's loop scores: loops active in the run, with their dominance
and the polarity the run shows.

The model's structure, because no loop was active in the run: loops
with their equations' polarity, and no dominance.

PartitionReport.description:
A cycle partition: stocks connected by feedback, and the loops among them,
which compete for dominance with each other and no others.

stocks.description:
Its stocks, as the model names them (an arrayed stock by element); at
most 12. Empty for the loops that pass through no stock of this model
(inside a module, or closed through a lagged value): each of those
stands alone, so they have no timeline and no shares.

otherStocks.description: How many more stocks it has than it names.

loopCount.description:
How many of its loops the analysis has (through `through`, when
given).

dominance.description:
Which loops led, span by span: the run's saved steps from its start to
its end, cut at the steps the lead changed, in at most 12 spans (the
shortest joined to their neighbours past that), each from the time of
its first step to the time of its last. With `through`, which of the
loops through it led. Absent for loops from structure.

loops.description:
Every loop `dominance` names, then the most important others (the
shortest, from structure); at most 8 besides those it names.

DominanceSpan.description:
A span of a run and the loops that led it: first the loop with the
largest share over the span, then its rivals, those holding at least half
its share there, strongest first; at most 3 in all. None led a span in
which no loop (through `through`, when given) was the strongest. A span
names the single strongest loop, so where several loops take over
together (SIR's balancing loops after the epidemic's peak) the span
changes a few steps after the turn, when one of them alone passes the
loop that led before.

share.description:
Its share of the partition's loop activity over the span, from 0 to 1:
at each time the shares of all the partition's loops sum to 1, so
where many loops are active each holds little.

id.description:
The session's id for this loop (`L1`, ...), the same in every run and
revision while the loop exists.

name.description: The name the model gives the loop, if it has one.

length.description: How many variables the loop passes through.

chain.description:
The loop from a stock (when it has one) around to where it started:
each step is a variable and the sign of the link from it to the next
step's variable, the last step's link returning to the first. Absent
for a loop of more than 12 variables, unless it was asked for by id.

stocks.description:
The stocks the loop passes through, in its order: given for a loop
whose chain is not.

share.description:
Its share of the partition's loop activity, from 0 to 1, averaged over
the steps at which the partition was active: the shares of a
partition's loops sum to 1. Absent for loops from structure, and for a
loop in no partition.

LoopPolarityName.description:
A loop's polarity: reinforcing (it amplifies change) or balancing (it
counteracts change). From a run, a loop that showed both is "mostly" the
one it showed at least 99% of the time, weighted by its score, and
undetermined otherwise; from structure, a loop with a link whose sign the
engine cannot tell is undetermined.

variable.description:
The variable, as the model names it; an element of an arrayed one is
subscripted.

polarity.description:
The sign of the link from this variable to the next: the run's, when
the run scored the link, so `?` there means its sign changed over the
run; otherwise its equation's.

via.description:
The builtins or macros the link passes through in the next variable's
equation (`smth1`, `delay3`), when it does: such a link carries a
delay, and is another link than a direct one between the same two
variables.

LinkPolarityName.description:
A link's sign as system dynamics writes it: `+` when the target moves with
the source, `-` when against it, `?` when the engine cannot tell from the
equation.

InactiveLoops.description: The model's loops that are not among a run's.

loops.description: The shortest of them, with their equations' signs; at most 8.

OmittedLoops.description: Loops the analysis has and the answer does not list.

loops.description:
Loops not listed, in listed partitions and the others. `through` finds
the loops through a variable.

links.description:
The links the replaced equations removed: what each replaced variable
read before and no longer reads.

loops.description:
The model's loops through them, which this run does not have; at most
8.

through.description: The variable `through` named, as the model names it.

found.description:
The loops the analysis has (those through `through`, when given): the
loops active in the run, or, from structure, the model's.

complete.description:
Whether those are every such loop. False when the analysis left out
loops that never held a thousandth of their partition's activity;
when it kept only the most important of the run's loops; when the
model has too many to enumerate, so the run's were found by searching
for the strongest (a sample); when the model has too many for its
structure alone to list; or when it has a conveyor or a queue, whose
loops are not analyzed.
That no loop goes through a variable is shown only from every loop
of the model: a complete analysis, or the active loops with the
`inactive` ones, where the structure lists them.

partitions.description: The partitions the loops are in, largest first.

inactive.description:
The model's loops, from its structure, that are not among this run's
(those through `through`, when given): inactive in it, or among those
the analysis left out. Absent when the run has every loop of the
model, from structure, and when the model has too many loops for its
structure alone to list.

absent.description:
Loops asked for by id that the run's analysis does not have, active,
inactive or cut: a loop of another revision of the model. A loop
asked for that is inactive in the run or cut from it is listed whole
under `inactive` or `cut`.

leftOut.description:
Loops asked for by id left out to keep the answer within its budget:
ask for them in another call.

cut.description: What the run's replaced equations cut.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Runs the validation battery, the model tests of system dynamics practice: the engine's unit check; extreme conditions (each constant at its low and its high extreme, chosen by what the constant is and said with each check, or the ones the call gives: values that become NaN or infinite, stocks that go below a zero they should not pass, in the model's own run too); integration error (the run at half and a quarter of the DT: the error at the model's DT, or that the model is discrete or chaotic); sensitivity (each constant at half and double: a change of behavior); loop knockouts (a named variable held at its initial value: the loops that cuts); disturbances (a step in a constant: the response, and the loops that lead after it). Unit conversions are left out unless named. Each check that did not pass comes with an id (T1, T2, ...) that claims can cite. Run it before judging a model.

ExtremeInput.description:
The extremes a call gives one constant; the one it leaves out is the
battery's.

low.description: The low extreme (for an arrayed constant, every element's).

high.description: The high extreme (for an arrayed constant, every element's).

tests.description: The tests to run: all of them when absent.

targets.description:
The variables the targeted tests change, in place of their defaults:
extreme conditions, sensitivity and disturbance take constants (the
constants that feed the model's flows by default, less its unit
conversions); a loop knockout holds variables at their initial
values, and runs only on targets named here. At most 12.

record.description:
The variables whose responses sensitivity, knockouts and disturbances
report: the model's stocks when absent. At most 12.

extremes.description:
Extremes for the extreme conditions test to give a constant in place
of the ones its rules choose, for a constant whose meaningful range
the model's author knows. A constant named here is a target of that
test whether or not `targets` names it. At most 12.

skipped.description: Why the test made no checks.

note.description:
What the test's outcomes rest on that its checks do not say: the
checks that found something only at the model's DT, or that were not
run again at a finer one.

TestResult.description: One check: what it changed, how it came out, and what it found.

id.description:
The session's id for this check (`T1`, ...), the same when it is run
again.

variable.description: The variable it changed, as the model names it.

extreme.description:
The rule that chose an extreme conditions check's value: if the rule
does not fit the constant, the check tested the wrong extreme, and the
call can give its own.

timeConstant.description: Why a check at a short time took its constant for a time constant.

heldAt.description:
The extreme a sensitivity check's half or double would have passed,
and was held at: the value tried is not half or double the
constant's.

value.description: The value it gave the variable (a scalar).

fromTime.description: When the change took effect (a disturbance).

problems.description: What went wrong in the run (extreme conditions), first first.

differences.description:
The stocks (or elements) whose values depend most on DT (integration
error).

order.description:
The order the runs at finer DTs converge at (integration error): about
1 for Euler and 4 for RK4 on a smooth model, and near or below 0 where
refining DT does not converge.

responses.description:
How recorded variables responded (sensitivity, knockout,
disturbance): those the check made undefined, then those whose
behavior changed materially, then the largest changes; at most three.

moreChanges.description:
How many more recorded series the check made undefined or changed
the behavior of materially than `responses` lists: `record` names the
ones to read.

sameChange.description:
The other sensitivity checks that flag the same change of the same
series, folded into this one.

loops.description:
Loop ids: those a knockout cut, or those that led after a
disturbance.

reason.description: Why a check did not run.

note.description:
What the outcome rests on that its numbers do not show: a
non-negative marking this engine does not enforce, why runs at finer
DTs do not converge, the time constant DT is too large for.

oneOf.description:
The model fails the check: fix the model, or say why the check does
not apply.
The check could not run; its reason says why.
A result for judgment: it may be right, and a modeler should say.
What happened, for an explanation: a knockout's or a disturbance's.
A constant at its low extreme; the check's `extreme` says which.
A constant at its high extreme; the check's `extreme` says which.
The model's own run, with nothing changed.

A constant at half its value (a time constant no lower than its low
extreme).

A constant at double its value (a share or a fractional rate no
higher than its high extreme).
The run at half and at a quarter of its DT.

A variable held at its initial value, each element of an arrayed one
at its own.
A constant stepped up by a tenth, a tenth of the way into the run.

ExtremeRule.description: The rule that chose an extreme conditions check's value.

oneOf.description: Low: zero, for a constant no equation divides by.

Low: a tenth of its value, for a constant some equation divides
by, whose domain zero is outside.

Low: a tenth of a time constant's value, and at least four DTs for
each of its stages (in its own unit of time).
Low: the run's start, for a date.
High: ten times its value.
High: the whole, for a share or fraction: 1, or 100 in percent.

High: ten times a fractional rate's value, and at most one over two
DTs (in its own unit of time).
High: past the run's stop, for a date.
The value the call gave.

TimeConstantEvidence.description:
Why the battery took a constant for a time constant, whose low extreme is
a short time rather than zero.

oneOf.description: Its units are a unit of time.
It is the time of a delay, smooth or trend.

It has no units, and divides a quantity a stock moves into a rate:
`(goal - level) / adjustment_time`.

It has no units, and its reciprocal multiplies a quantity a stock
moves into a rate: `population * (1 / lifetime)`, or `population *
death_fraction` with `death_fraction = 1 / lifetime`.

variable.description: The variable (or element), as the model names it.

nonNegative.description:
Whether the model marks it non-negative. The engine does not enforce
the marking, so it goes negative here where a tool that enforces it
would hold it at zero.

oneOf.description: A value became NaN or infinite.
A value went below zero that does not in the model's run.

difference.description:
Its estimated error at the model's DT, as a fraction of its scale (the
larger of its range and its largest magnitude): its largest
difference from the run at half the DT, extrapolated by the order the
runs converge at; where they do not converge, that difference itself.

change.description:
How far its final value moved from the model's run, as a fraction of
its scale there (of what it is computed from, for a series the
model's run holds at zero): positive up, negative down. Left out when either run
of the series is not a number somewhere, which its mode says.

largestChange.description:
Its largest difference from the model's run at any time, as a
fraction of its scale there. Left out as `change` is.

mode.description: Its behavior mode in the check's run.

was.description: Its behavior mode in the model's run, when the check changed it.

damping.description:
Whether its swings die out, hold or grow in the check's run, when it
oscillates there: a loss of stability shows here.

wasDamping.description: The same in the model's run, when the check changed it.

family.description:
The family of its behavior in the check's run, when the check changed
it materially: its mode with pace set aside, so a label can change
while the family stays (exponential growth that reads as linear over
a shorter horizon, a goal seeker a few percent past its goal).

wasFamily.description:
The family of its behavior in the model's run, when the check
changed it.

oneOf.description: Does not move: an equilibrium.
Moves at a steady speed.
Moves ever faster: exponential growth, or an accelerating decline.
Moves ever slower toward a level: approach to a goal, or decay.
Speeds up, then slows toward a level.

Passes the level it ends at, and comes back less than half the way it
went.

Rises, peaks, and falls back more than half the way it rose: overshoot
and collapse.
Falls, bottoms, and rises back more than half the way it fell.
Swings back and forth.
Takes a non-finite value.
None of these.
Each swing smaller than the last.
Swings of about the same size.
Each swing larger than the last.
Too few swings in the run to tell.

BehaviorFamily.description:
A behavior's family: what a change of behavior means, as the classifier's
label does not. Which of linear, exponential, goal seeking or S-shaped
growth a series reads as depends on the horizon as much as on the
structure: they are one family, which a change of pace does not leave.

oneOf.description: It does not move.
It rises, without a material turn.
It falls, without a material turn.
It rises, turns once, and falls.
It falls, turns once, and rises.
It turns twice or more.

SameChange.description: A sensitivity check folded into another that flags the same change.

suggestions.description: The closest names of variables, when no variable has the name.

reason.description:
Why not, when the variable exists and what was asked of it does not:
an element it does not have, or a subscript on a variable with none.

tests.description: Each test run, with how its checks came out.

results.description:
The checks worth reading, each under its id: every one that did not
pass, and sensitivity's strongest; failures first.

omitted.description:
Checks worth reading that the answer leaves out, past its limit or
its budget.

runFails.description:
Why the model's own run fails, when it does: every test that runs the
model is skipped.

leftOut.description:
What the default targets of the tests leave out, and why: the unit
conversions, and the dates sensitivity and disturbance do not scale.

tools.name: edit_model
tools.description: Edits the model: add stocks, flows and variables, set equations, units, notes and lookups, connect flows, rename, delete, name loops, change the sim specs. The edit is made when its gate passes, and the answer lists what changed and the warnings it added. The gate refuses an edit, changing nothing, that would add an error anywhere in the project, leave an error in an equation it writes, stop the model simulating, make a value not a number, or give a model its first unit warning. Read the model first: an edit of something that changed since you read it is refused, naming what changed.

EditOperation.description:
One operation of an edit. An equation names a variable as the equation
language spells it: `room_heat`, or `"Room Heat"` in quotes, for a
variable shown as Room Heat.

oneOf.description:
Add a stock with its initial value, and the flows (existing ones, or
ones added earlier in this edit) that fill and drain it.

Add a flow with its equation, draining the stock `from` and filling
the stock `to`; a side left out is a cloud, outside the model.
Add an auxiliary: a constant, or a variable computed from others.

Replace a variable's equation (a stock's: its initial value). For an
arrayed variable, the equation applies to every element, or to the
one `element` names (`north`; `north, young` for an element of several
dimensions).
Set a variable's units; empty clears them.
Set a variable's documentation; empty clears it.

Make a variable a lookup of its equation: `points` are `[x, y]` pairs,
x never decreasing (two points at one x are a vertical step).

kind.description:
How it reads between and past its points: continuous (the
default: interpolated, held at the ends), extrapolate, or
discrete (stepped).

oneOf.description:
Set which stock a flow drains (`from`) and fills (`to`); a side left
out is a cloud.

Rename a variable; every equation that reads it is rewritten. A new
name that differs only in case or spacing changes how the name is
written and nothing else.

Delete a variable; a deleted flow leaves the stocks it filled and
drained, and a module input it fed is left unwired.

Name a feedback loop, by the id analyze_loops gave it or by its
variables.
Change the run's start, stop, DT or integration method.

LookupShape.description: How a lookup reads between and past its points.

summary.description:
What the edit does and why, in a sentence: what the person whose
model it is reads of it, beside its undo.

operations.description:
The operations, applied in order: each sees the ones before it. At
most 24.

variable.description:
The variable, as the model names it (before a rename; with its model
when it is another model's), a loop's name, or "sim specs".

EditDiagnostic.description: A diagnostic the edit adds or leaves, or would.

id.description:
The session's id for it (`D1`, ...), the one `read_model` reports it
under, so a finding can cite it: present once the edit is made, for a
diagnostic of the model the edit is of.

model.description: The model it is in, when that is not the model the edit is of.

Severity.description: Whether a diagnostic stops the model from simulating or only warns.

DiagnosticCategoryName.description:
Where a diagnostic was raised, named for a reader: one per category of
the engine's (`DiagnosticCategory`).

oneOf.description:
An equation that does not parse, names something that does not
exist, or cannot be compiled.

A problem with the model as a whole: a cycle, a duplicate name, a bad
table.
A units string that does not parse.
An equation whose computed units disagree with its declared units.
A contradiction among the units the model's equations imply.
A construct the compiler refuses.

A value a run produces that is not a number: what an edit's gate
finds in the run, where the engine's diagnostics are silent.

revision.description:
The revision of the model the edit was made on. The edited model has
a revision of its own, which the host gives it and the next read
reports.

changes.description:
One line per variable the edit changes, in any model of the project,
and for the sim specs and loop names. A line's detail is cut at 240
characters.

omitted.description: Lines left out to keep the answer within its budget.

omittedDiagnostics.description:
Diagnostics left out to keep the answer within its budget, the last
listed: a read lists them all.

unchanged.description:
That the model was already as the edit asks: nothing changed, and
there is no edit for the host to make.

diagnostics.description:
What the edit adds or leaves: every warning it adds (to fix), and an
error whose reason it changes, each under the id a read gives it.

simulates.description:
Whether the model simulates as the edit leaves it; absent when the
edit changed nothing (`unchanged`), which compiles and runs nothing.

note.description: Anything else that needs saying of the edit.

tools.name: verify_findings
tools.description: Checks the evidence of findings before the person sees them. A finding is a flaw, a strength or an observation, a claim in a sentence or two, and the citations it rests on: a variable, its equation, the variables that read it, a link, a diagnostic id, a loop id and its polarity, a loop leading over a span of a run, a run fact (a value at a time, goes negative, peaks at, ends near, behavior mode), a comparison of two runs, an absence (no diagnostics, no loop through a variable, no readers), or a battery check's outcome. A finding whose every citation holds gets an id (F1, F2, ...) and may be shown; each citation that fails says what is true instead. Cite only what the tools reported.

claim.description: The claim, in a sentence or two, as the person will read it.

citations.description:
The evidence: at least one, at most 8, each naming something a tool
reported.

oneOf.description: Something wrong with the model.
Something the model does well.
What the model does, neither.

Citation.description:
One piece of evidence. `run` is "current" (the model as it is) when
absent; a variable of a run may be an element (`Population[north]`).

oneOf.description: The model has the variable.

The variable's equation (a stock's: its initial value) is `equation`,
written any way that parses the same: spacing, case and the spelling
of names aside. For an arrayed variable, name an element it has
(`Population[north]`) for that element's equation. A variable with a
table is its table at its equation's value: `LOOKUP(effect, input)`,
not `input`. A table with no equation of its own, which other
equations look up, is cited with an empty equation.

The variable (or one element of it) is within 5% of `value` at `time`
in the run (of the larger of the two); a `value` of zero holds for a
value under a hundred-thousandth of the series' largest. At the run's
start when `time` is absent, which for a constant is its value. A
time outside the run is refused.

The variables that read `variable` -- those whose equations read it in
any phase, an initial value or `INIT` included, those that look it up
as a table, a stock or flow whose option names it (a conveyor's
transit time), and for a flow the stocks it fills and drains -- are
exactly `readers`: none, when it is empty, for a variable nothing
reads. It cannot hold while an equation of the model does not parse,
since that equation may read it.

`variable` reads `reads`, through a link of `polarity` (its equation's
sign) when given.
The model has the diagnostic of this id now.
The model has no diagnostic of `category`, or none at all.

The run has the loop of this id, of `polarity` when given (a mostly
reinforcing loop is reinforcing, a mostly balancing one balancing).

The loop was its partition's strongest for most of the steps between
`from` and `to` in which a loop was active.
No loop of the run goes through the variable.

The variable (an element of it, for an arrayed one) goes below zero
in the run: exactly when its summary says when it went negative.

The variable peaks at `time`, within 5% of the run: it is at its
largest there, and lower at the run's start and at its end. A series
still rising when the run ends, or falling from its start, has no
peak in the run.
The variable ends within 5% of `value`, judged as `value` judges one.
The variable's behavior mode in the run is `mode`.
The variable ends higher (or lower) in `run` than in `than`.

The battery check of this id comes out `outcome`, run again when the
model has changed since.

LinkPolarityName.description:
A link's sign as system dynamics writes it: `+` when the target moves with
the source, `-` when against it, `?` when the engine cannot tell from the
equation.

DiagnosticCategoryName.description:
Where a diagnostic was raised, named for a reader: one per category of
the engine's (`DiagnosticCategory`).

oneOf.description:
An equation that does not parse, names something that does not
exist, or cannot be compiled.

A problem with the model as a whole: a cycle, a duplicate name, a bad
table.
A units string that does not parse.
An equation whose computed units disagree with its declared units.
A contradiction among the units the model's equations imply.
A construct the compiler refuses.

A value a run produces that is not a number: what an edit's gate
finds in the run, where the engine's diagnostics are silent.

LoopPolarityName.description:
A loop's polarity: reinforcing (it amplifies change) or balancing (it
counteracts change). From a run, a loop that showed both is "mostly" the
one it showed at least 99% of the time, weighted by its score, and
undetermined otherwise; from structure, a loop with a link whose sign the
engine cannot tell is undetermined.

oneOf.description: Does not move: an equilibrium.
Moves at a steady speed.
Moves ever faster: exponential growth, or an accelerating decline.
Moves ever slower toward a level: approach to a goal, or decay.
Speeds up, then slows toward a level.

Passes the level it ends at, and comes back less than half the way it
went.

Rises, peaks, and falls back more than half the way it rose: overshoot
and collapse.
Falls, bottoms, and rises back more than half the way it fell.
Swings back and forth.
Takes a non-finite value.
None of these.

Relation.description: A final value's relation between two runs.

oneOf.description:
The model fails the check: fix the model, or say why the check does
not apply.
The check could not run; its reason says why.
A result for judgment: it may be right, and a modeler should say.
What happened, for an explanation: a knockout's or a disturbance's.

id.description:
The finding's id (`F1`, ...) when every citation holds: what the host
shows it under.

failures.description:
The citations that do not hold, by their place in the finding (from
1), each with what is true instead.

omittedFailures.description:
Failures left out, the last of the finding's, to keep the answer
within its budget.

findings.description: A verdict per finding, in the order given.

omitted.description:
The last findings, left out to keep the answer within its budget:
they get no id and no verdict here; verify them in a call of their
own.

RefusedEdit.description:
What a refusal of an edit by its gate carries beside its reason
(`refusedEdit` in the one refusal shape): the rule that refused it and
what the edit would have done, for the agent to repair its operations.
Nothing changed.

rule.description: The rule that refused the edit.

changes.description:
One line per variable the edit would have changed, as a made edit's
lines say them. A line's detail is cut at 240 characters.

omitted.description: Lines left out to keep the refusal within its budget.

omittedDiagnostics.description:
Diagnostics left out to keep the refusal within its budget, the last
listed.

diagnostics.description:
What the edit would add or leave: the errors it would add, an error
in an equation it writes, the values that would not be a number, the
first unit warning of a model without one, and the warnings it would
add. None has an id: they are of no model.

simulates.description: Whether the model would simulate as the edit would leave it.

GateRule.description: A rule of the gate, as a refusal names the one that refused an edit.

oneOf.description:
The edit adds an error the project did not have, in any of its
models, or leaves one in an equation it writes.
The edit's specs ask more of a run than a run may.

A model that simulated would not: the model the edit is of, or the
project's root model.

A value would not be a number where the run of the model as it is
has a number throughout.
A model without unit warnings would get its first.

variable.description:
The variable, as the model names it (before a rename; with its model
when it is another model's), a loop's name, or "sim specs".

EditDiagnostic.description: A diagnostic the edit adds or leaves, or would.

id.description:
The session's id for it (`D1`, ...), the one `read_model` reports it
under, so a finding can cite it: present once the edit is made, for a
diagnostic of the model the edit is of.

model.description: The model it is in, when that is not the model the edit is of.

Severity.description: Whether a diagnostic stops the model from simulating or only warns.

DiagnosticCategoryName.description:
Where a diagnostic was raised, named for a reader: one per category of
the engine's (`DiagnosticCategory`).

oneOf.description:
An equation that does not parse, names something that does not
exist, or cannot be compiled.

A problem with the model as a whole: a cycle, a duplicate name, a bad
table.
A units string that does not parse.
An equation whose computed units disagree with its declared units.
A contradiction among the units the model's equations imply.
A construct the compiler refuses.

A value a run produces that is not a number: what an edit's gate
finds in the run, where the engine's diagnostics are silent.

refusalSchema.title: Refusal
refusalSchema.description:
A refusal: what rule the call broke and how to repair it. Every tool
refuses in this one shape, which the catalog publishes beside the tools'
own schemas (`refusalSchema`).

error.description: The rule the call broke, and the repair.

suggestions.description: Names the call may have meant: variables, models or runs.

interrupted.description:
That the call stopped for other work on the project and kept nothing:
what a host that retries by itself looks for. It retries once that
work is done -- after an edit, at the next revision -- and never in a
loop against a project that stays busy.

cancelled.description:
That the host cancelled the call, which stopped and kept nothing: no
host calls it again.

refusedEdit.description:
For an edit its gate refused: the rule that refused it and what the
edit would have done, for the agent to repair its operations.
